source.title: Localizing Safety Alignment: MLP Layers and Mid-Network Blocks Encode Refusal Behavior in Large Language Models
source.authors: Mingyu Zong; Sampad Mohanty; Bhaskar Krishnamachari

record.file_problem: none; the full paper is present. Some table text is flattened, but the reported values used below can be assigned from the table layout and accompanying text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether refusal behavior is localized in a small set of parameters using aligned-to-base weight transplantation and behavioral refusal measures, rather than the original studies’ fine-tuning or per-token KL methods.
record.gate_note: The paper tests weight-space localization and refusal transfer, not harmful- or benign-data fine-tuning, per-token KL concentration, prompt-opening bypasses, or why safety is shallow. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows. It reports additional individual-block, block-budget, and OR-Bench results; the rows_left_out field identifies omitted results.
record.test_reason: It uses aligned-to-base weight transplantation, a different method from pruning or rank ablation, to ask whether a localized set of weights carries refusal (V5). The outcome is manually judged refusal counts on prompts filtered so the aligned model refuses and the base model complies. It does not test V1–V4, V6 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is mostly right. In two 7–8B pairs, transferable refusal is carried mainly by MLP weights (at least 2.7x attention), and Block 3 (layers 8–11) is selected first in all six greedy searches. Block effects are non-additive, and selective subsets can beat full MLP transplantation. The authors add that refusal and over-refusal are co-localized, and that greedy orders transfer to OR-Bench differently depending on the source benchmark. Their validation establishes robustness only within the filtered distribution.
record.recipe_differences: Uses aligned-to-base weight transplantation and benchmark refusal counts to localize transferable behavior; does not use few-example fine-tuning or per-token KL analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model pair, benchmark, selected block set, and benchmark-specific greedy order; full transplantation is not consistently best.

fits_no_version.finding: For RealSafe-R1-7B, the MLP transplant that transfers the most harmful-prompt refusal also transfers the most benign over-refusal: 11/30 on TwinPrompt and 33/100 on validation, versus at most 7 elsewhere. The saferlhf MLP transplant shows 0/5 TwinPrompt BOR. OR-Bench over-refusal varies with which benchmark the greedy order was derived from.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weights that carry transferable refusal also carry over-refusal; the two are co-localized and not cleanly separable at the component level.

record.problems: Only two matched 7B–8B model pairs; primary subsets have at most 30 prompts and are filtered for aligned–base disagreement. The 100-prompt validation remains filtered. No uncertainty estimates are reported, and the authors note greedy forward selection only approximates the space of block combinations.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted component-level results for first5, mid5, last5, first-half, and second-half configurations on the original 30-prompt benchmarks; Tables 2–4. Omitted most individual-block results other than Block 3; Tables 3–4 and 11. Omitted intermediate greedy budgets and BOR values from Tables 6–7, and OR-Bench block-order results in Table 8. These were left out to stay within 60 rows while retaining the main MLP/attention comparisons, Block 3 results, key non-monotonic comparisons, and the larger validation results.

untested.parts: The study does not test: localization by removal or ablation in the aligned model; rank or low-rank localization; what fraction of parameters is involved (MLP is most of each layer's weights); and whether the localized weights explain brittleness under fine-tuning. It covers only two 7–8B pairs, and all evaluations are on aligned–base disagreement-filtered prompts.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
No test of data or objective as the cause.

missing.what: Layer-level results within Block 3 for RealSafe. Layer 8 alone gives 3/30, 5/30 and 6/30 refusals, near or above half the full block (7, 3, 10). Layer subsets can match or exceed the full block. This is the finest-grained localization evidence for V5.

saferlhf ultra sft component-level TwinPrompt BOR (0/5 for all configs, including mlp), and the 30-prompt coarse-region results for both pairs. For saferlhf, first half gives 18/30 on TwinPrompt while second half gives 0/30.

record.verdict_notes: Transplantation tests whether aligned weights are sufficient to transfer refusal into the base model, not whether they are necessary in the aligned model. The 'localized' set the paper emphasizes is the whole MLP pathway, which is a large share of parameters; truly small subsets (one block, one layer) transfer only a minority of refusal. Baselines are 0 and the aligned model is at ceiling by construction of the filtered subsets (at most 30 prompts; 100 in validation). There are no uncertainty estimates, judging is manual, and sampling is at temperature 0.6. Greedy rows are selected on the same subsets they are evaluated on, so the subset-beats-full comparisons are in-sample.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or measurement of harmful fine-tuning’s effect.
No fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully selected benign data.
No compliant-opening prefills, suffix attacks, or decoding-change tests.

Tests transfer of refusal through selected weight transplants, not whether safety is intrinsically carried by a small set of weights under removal, fine-tuning, or other interventions; only two matched model pairs are studied.
No test of whether training data or objective causes shallow safety.
No training designed to deepen safety or test of whether such training holds up.

source_check.notes: Results concern explicit refusal on filtered aligned–base disagreement prompts; they do not establish sparse individual weights or general capability preservation. Table 7 lists a saferlhf AdvBench full-transplant endpoint of 12/30, conflicting with Table 2's 17/30 and the monotonic-trajectory narrative.

statements.correction: RealSafe Block 3: 7/30 TwinPrompt, 3/30 SGXSTest, 10/30 AdvBench refusals; saferlhf individual blocks: at most 2/30. Appropriate label for incomplete single-block transfer: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The numerical summary is correct, but the challenges label overstates this study's evidence: weak or incomplete transfer qualifies localization rather than showing it absent across the stated condition group.
